 AGP for the Appellant : Shri S.R.Yadav.
Advocate for the Respondents : Shri Dixit Sushant V..

...
 CORAM: RAVINDRA V. GHUGE, J.
DATE :- 12th February, 2019
1 The objections raised by the learned Advocate for the Respondents as regards the maintainability of this Appeal from Order, were considered.
2 My attention was drawn to Sections 68 to 71 under Chapter X of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 pertaining to the adjudication by the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal.

Under Section 68, the Adjudicating Officer, who is to be designated by the State Government and who is not to be below the rank of the Additional District Magistrate of the district, is vested with the powers of the civil court and all proceedings before him shall be deemed to be judicial proceedings within the meaning of Sections *2* 908ao9o19 193 and 228 of the Indian Penal Code.
It is also provided that it would be deemed to be a court for the purposes of Sections 345 and 346 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
3 Proviso below Section 69(3) indicates that no offence, for which punishment of imprisonment has been prescribed under this Act, shall be compounded.

Section 70 deals with the establishment of the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal and Section 71 confers powers on the said Tribunal specifically indicating in sub-section (1) that the The State Of Maharashtra Through Food ... vs Pankaj Gupta, Nominee, Adani Wilmar ... on 12 February, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197323078/

sentences.text: Tribunal shall not be bound by the procedure laid down by the Code of Criminal Procedure, but shall be guided by the principles of natural justice, though under sub-section (2) the Tribunal shall have the power to discharge its functions under the said Act having the same powers as are vested in the civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure with regard to recording of evidence.

4 The learned AGP has specifically relied upon the judgment of the Allahabad High Court in the matter of Pradeep Kumar Gupta vs. State of U.P., 2015 (3) ACR 2924 :
2015 (6) ADJ 351 : 2016 Cri.L.J. 122, wherein, it has been concluded that an appeal under Section 70(1) of the 2006 Act, against the decision of the adjudicating officer under Section 68, before the Food Safe Appellate Tribunal would be treated as a Civil Miscellaneous Appeal and not a criminal appeal.

5 The learned Advocate for the Respondents submits that he would cause research on this aspect in order to look up to judicial pronouncements of this Court or the Honourable Supreme Court, if any.
6 In view of the above, stand over to 06.03.2019 in the urgent admissions category.
